_meta.note: This file is the ONLY mode table. Every GENUINELY NEW rule starts advisory. Promotion to gate is a one-line edit here, per rule, once its openBacklog reaches 0 and every remaining baseline entry carries a real human reason (Bean-locked, 2026-08-03). No prose-cached backlog counts elsewhere — run `node run.js --json` for the live number. EXCEPTION (added 2026-08-05, Spec 35 Task C migration): rules 04/08/14/17 are a VERBATIM PORT of audit-inspector-conformance.js's four warn-severity rules, which is already wired into `prebuild` as a hard `--check` gate today — porting them straight to `mode:"gate"` PRESERVES current enforcement (0 net backlog, matching the OLD script's own live output the same day) rather than starting a new backlog count at advisory. Rules 03/07 are that same OLD script's two `informational`-severity rules, which NEVER contributed to its gate exit code by design (audit-inspector-conformance.js:591-596) — those port to `mode:"advisory"` for the identical reason: preserving current (non-)enforcement exactly, not silently adding a new gate that never existed. See each rule file's own header for the independent population cross-check.
_meta.zeroIsAClaim: A rule returning ZERO findings on the live tree is a claim requiring evidence, not a pass (Bean-locked, 2026-08-03, after coordinator review caught rule 01 counting <InspectorControls> elements instead of panels and silently missing 42+ real unrouted blocks — including hero, the specific block flagged as unusable). Whoever adds a rule MUST: (1) state its expected population BEFORE trusting a live run, using a method independent of the rule's own code — a second script in a different style, a manual grep, or a hand count; (2) if the rule returns 0 or a suspiciously round/small number, treat that as a red flag and re-derive the condition from what the checklist item actually requires, not from what was easy to detect in one file; (3) record the comparison (expected vs actual) somewhere reviewable before setting the rule's advisoryReason. All three shipped rules here (01/18/20) were cross-checked this way on 2026-08-03: 01 measured 65 (was silently 0 under the first, wrong condition), 18 measured 15 (was 12 before a shared-component blind spot — MediaPicker.js — was found and fixed), 20 measured 23 (was 43 before a wrong exclusion mechanism — filename prefix instead of the pattern's own 'Post Types:' header — was found and fixed).

rules.advisoryReason: PORTED from audit-inspector-conformance.js's preset-only-shadow rule — `informational` severity in the OLD script, NEVER gated the build. Ported straight to advisory to preserve that exact non-enforcement (see rules.json _meta.note EXCEPTION clause). Measured live 2026-08-05: 1/84 blocks (sgs/post-grid, edit.js:882, label="Hover shadow") — a SelectControl labelled with the word 'shadow'. Independently cross-checked with a standalone Babel walk: 1/1 match. The architecture doc marks this rule 'fuzzy today: label regex' and keeps it advisory even in the target end-state until a ShadowControl-resolution detector replaces the label-text heuristic — not absorbed in this port. ⛔ RAISED 0 -> 1 ON 2026-08-19, DELIBERATELY, WITH THE REAL FIX NAMED. sgs/site-header mounted a shadow control (Bean-ruled: the `shadow` attribute was declared AND rendered by SGS_Container_Wrapper, but no control had ever been mounted, so no client could reach a working feature). It uses the preset SelectControl + SHADOW_OPTIONS, which is what this rule flags. The real builder was NOT used, and the reason is mechanical rather than preference: ShadowControl stores SHAPE ONLY and requires the CALLER to own a sibling `{name}Colour` attribute composed at render by sgs_shadow_value_composed(). The header renders its shadow through SGS_Container_Wrapper, whose shadow path is the older shape-only sgs_shadow_value() (class-sgs-container-wrapper.php:892) with NO colour composition at all. Mounting the real builder here would therefore ship a colour field the wrapper ignores — a dead control, strictly worse than a preset select that works. Note sgs/container mounts the IDENTICAL preset select and is not flagged only because it lives in a shared component file this rule does not scan, so the header is consistent with every other wrapper block, not an outlier. THE REAL FIX: migrate the wrapper's shadow path to sgs_shadow_value_composed() + a wrapper-level shadowColour attribute, after which every wrapper block (container included) can move to ShadowControl in one pass. That is a shared-mechanism change and needs its own design gate — it is not this task.

rules.advisoryReason: ⬆ RAISED 199 -> 211 (2026-08-24), Bean's explicit call, and it is a STALENESS CORRECTION rather than accepted new debt. 199 was set on 2026-08-08 in the commit that CREATED this rule (76f44a1d) and was never re-measured. This rule's OWN advisoryReason below already records 'CURRENT STATE (2026-08-19): 200 FLAGGED + 11 BASELINED' = 211 — so the declared ceiling has been below the measured tree since at least five days after it was written, and every blocks build has been failing on it. Measured 211 immediately before AND immediately after an unrelated 18-file change (block.json flexWrap defaults + the container wrapper), confirming the figure is settled and that change contributed zero. ⚠ RESOLVED 2026-08-27, and the suspicion was BACKWARDS. The comparison is not defective. run.js:203 computes flagged = findings.filter(status===FLAGGED).length and :204 tests flagged > cap, so the ratchet is FLAGGED-ONLY on both sides. Baselining a finding REMOVES it from the compared number, which LOOSENS the gate - it can never re-trip it, which is what the earlier note feared. Measured this day across the full scan: FLAGGED 211, BASELINED 11, TOTAL 222. The ceiling of 211 therefore sits EXACTLY on the live FLAGGED count with ZERO slack, so it binds tightly and one new violation reds the build. The 222 that circulates in the planning docs is FLAGGED+BASELINED - the exact over-count the WHEN RE-MEASURING box below warns about, so quote 211 and never 222. One caveat left standing, not investigated here: if the 2026-08-19 figure recorded below (200 FLAGGED + 11 BASELINED) is accurate, then raising the ceiling to 211 on a FLAGGED+BASELINED basis left 11 of slack, and FLAGGED has since grown 200 -> 211 to fill exactly that gap - i.e. 11 findings may have landed green inside it. That is the documented failure mode of slack, and it is stated here as a possibility because the 200 has not been independently re-derived. The ratchet still binds from 211 downward. --- CURRENT STATE (2026-08-19): 200 FLAGGED + 11 BASELINED across 83 blocks. NOT promotable — 200 is a large real backlog and a smaller number was never the goal. WHAT IT DETECTS: the exact complement of check-dead-controls.js CHECK 4, which fires only when there is no control AND no render — so this whole quadrant (rendered, but no control) is invisible to it by construction. The dominant real family: a block that passes its whole attributes array to SGS_Container_Wrapper::render() inherits the wrapper's entire attribute vocabulary as rendered, so every container/grid/background attr it declares without a control is frozen at its block.json default forever. ⛔ WHEN RE-MEASURING, COUNT status="FLAGGED" ONLY. core/report.js:96-101 serialises BASELINED findings into the --json array too, while printHuman (:50,:59) and computeExit (run.js:168) filter to FLAGGED — a raw array length over-counts by exactly the baselined entries. COMPONENT RESOLUTION: delegated to core/components.js resolveComponentFiles() since 2026-08-19 (C0) — one shared mechanism, not a private copy that can disagree with no way to arbitrate. It indexes every name a file EXPORTS plus its filename, across src/components/, src/blocks/*/components/ and src/blocks/extensions/, and resolves collisions by PRECEDENCE: a file that DECLARES a name beats one that only RE-EXPORTS it. That precedence rule is load-bearing, not cosmetic — the 2026-08-17 panel split (D655) left ContainerWrapperControls.js a 268-line facade re-exporting the six panels, and under the previous first-wins-by-readdir-order it claimed LayoutPanel/WidthPanel/WrapperColourPanel while their attribute vocabulary had moved out, producing 50 false positives. A false positive is a detector bug, never baseline fodder. Transitive expansion is SCOPED PER EXPORT, never per file: exportBody() isolates the named export's own body and returns null rather than guessing, so the rule fails toward a false positive and never toward a silent suppression — a per-file attempt cleared site-header's and site-footer's five overlay findings each, which are genuinely real, trading 20 false positives for 10 false negatives. CORE-SUPPORTS EXCLUSION: nine attrs whose control WordPress core renders from the block's own supports (anchor, align, className via customClassName, color.background, color.text, …) live in the Advanced panel, alignment toolbar and Colour panel — none of which is in edit.js or any SGS component, so neither corpus can see them. Each mapping is cited to WP 7.0.3 core source in the rule header. ⛔ typography.textAlign is NOT among them: core reads the value from style.typography.textAlign (typography.php:184,246-247) and registers no named textAlign attribute, so a block declaring its own textAlign holds something core's control never writes — sgs/cta-section.textAlign is a REAL defect, pinned by fixture textalign-support-still-flags. BASELINED CLASSES (3), each left unfixed deliberately because the fix would touch machinery shared with other rules and silently restage their committed backlogs: comment-only matches (core/sources.js:151-156 strips only slash-star comments from PHP/CSS, so a double-slash line comment survives into the render corpus); variable-tail key construction (before-after/edit.js:241-245 builds tier keys with a literal fragment BETWEEN two interpolations, which no SUFFIX_SHAPE can reach); and one prose collision (testimonial-slider.testimonials matching the English word inside aria-label strings). FIXTURE NOTE: control-via-nested-shared-component guards transitive resolution against the REAL src/ tree, not the fixture copy. It was RED at HEAD until 2026-08-19 and was correct to be — GradientOverlayControl had been parameterised to attrNames=DEFAULT_ATTR_NAMES (:73-76), which owns only overlayGradient and backgroundOverlayColour, so the three overlayGradientAngle/From/To attrs the fixture also asserted were no longer owned by any shared component. The fixture's premise was corrected to the two names; the assertion is unchanged. HISTORY: superseded counts and their derivations are in git, not here — this field states the current truth only.

NEW 2026-08-09. Advisory FIRST per the advisory-before-fail-closed rule (E6 point 9): promote to blocking only after a cycle green on a real run, never on the run that introduces it. Measured at introduction: 0 findings across all 8 declared surfaces — but only after a FOURTH banned pattern was removed. That pattern banned "behaviour -> Settings; appearance -> Styles" and produced 1 false positive on its only two hits, both of which were the documentation RECORDING that rule's retirement ("amended from ...", "The retired rule was ..."). It also matched inconsistently, missing the same phrase where it was line-wrapped in the four extension files. A phrase that must be quoted to say it is retired cannot be banned by substring; the reasoning is kept in the rule file so it is not re-added. The three surviving patterns are assertive constructions that cannot occur inside a negation of themselves, which the surface-negates-retired-phrase fixture proves by carrying the corrected wording and requiring it NOT to flag. Promote by flipping mode to 'gate'. (⚠ this line previously said 'check' — 'check' is NOT an accepted mode; run.js:70 accepts gate|advisory|off only. Corrected 2026-08-10.)

NEW 2026-08-10, closing the gate D540 itself recorded as owed ('A gate asserting the rule is NOT built ... this meaning drifted silently on 5 blocks before anyone noticed'). Advisory FIRST per E6 point 9 — never promote on the run that introduces the rule. ⚠ READ THE PREDICTION AND ITS FALSIFICATION TOGETHER — the prediction was WRONG and the way it was wrong is the point. PREDICTED 1, MEASURED 3. The prediction (declared before the first live run per _meta.zeroIsAClaim) came from a shell census over src/blocks/*/block.json + render.php: 28 blocks declare contentWidth (D540's own 33 minus the 5 it deleted) and 'all 28 route through SGS_Container_Wrapper'. Two independent errors sat in that sentence. (a) D540's own conclusion that wrapper-routing implies a band is FALSE: three call sites override the guard via $opts['wrap_inner'] (class-sgs-container-wrapper.php:81,112) — physics-canvas/render.php:97 forces it TRUE (clean); hero/render.php:1065-1066 suppresses it for split but bands the content with centred padding-inline on the grid (:326-341), which is a REAL band and the correct mechanism there, since a grid item is sized by its track and a max-width on the column would be an inert lever (Bean-ruled 2026-08-10, correcting an earlier draft of this rule that WOULD have flagged hero); product-card/render.php:313 suppresses it unconditionally in the $base_opts every branch shares and reads contentWidth nowhere in code (only a docblock at :21), so the wrapper writes band CSS to a selector that never renders. (b) The census itself was wrong: it grepped for the string 'SGS_Container_Wrapper' and MATCHED COMMENTS. sgs/info-box and sgs/option-picker both DROPPED the wrapper under D294 and mention it only in prose explaining that they dropped it — so both were counted as wrapper-routed while actually rendering block-private, each emitting `width:` from contentWidth and `max-width:` from maxWidth onto the SAME root selector (info-box/render.php:299-304, option-picker/render.php:347-352). That is verbatim the shape D540 described and deleted from five blocks. Same 'a comment is not a call' trap this rule's own header warns about for the render side, committed on the census side by the person writing it. MEASURED THEREFORE 3: product-card (inert), info-box, option-picker. REMEDIES DIFFER BY EVIDENCE, per Bean 2026-08-10: product-card's contentWidth DELETED (inert; 0 theme patterns and 0 canary posts set it); info-box and option-picker RENAMED contentWidth -> width, keeping behaviour byte-identical, because D540's own text says a block that genuinely wants a fixed width says `width` and these two demonstrably do — info-box is live on two published canary pages at 900px and 480px, so deletion would have changed real pages, which is exactly why the theme+canary evidence was gathered before choosing. Post-remedy live run: 0 FLAGGED. The rule is proven able to FAIL against real code, not fixtures alone: contentWidth was temporarily restored to sgs/quote, the run reported 1 finding naming it, and the revert was confirmed on disk (0 occurrences, empty git diff) before the 0 was trusted. openBacklog 0 is therefore a measured zero on a rule that has demonstrably flagged live code three times.

NEW 2026-08-10. Advisory FIRST per E6 point 9 — never promote on the run that introduces the rule. Violators: sgs/button, 67 via the extension, 2 baselined"). The '2 baselined' belong to rule 08 (TextControl type="url") and are not duplicated here — this rule matches JSX component NAMES only. A colour/link control reached indirectly via a shared src/components/*.js file OTHER than the two canonical wrappers (e.g. GradientOverlayControl.js:191's raw GradientPicker, reaching container/hero/trust-bar/cta-section per §1.3/§1.7) is also out of scope — same per-block-edit.js boundary rules 04/08/18 already use, not an oversight. NEW 2026-08-10. Advisory FIRST per E6 point 9 — never promote on the run that introduces the rule. Guards contract §12's banned lookalike ('per-tier duplicate controls rendered side by side instead of one wrapped control') in the ONE corpus no existing detector reaches. NEW 2026-08-18. Spec 35 F.1: a composite's selectors.typography must target its own ROOT, never a child's dead BEM class. Guards the THIRD defect layer (declared / rendered / CONSUMED) that no other rule checks: a native typography control can exist, render, and save a value while its generated CSS never reaches the painted element. WORKED EXAMPLE: sgs/hero's 7 declared native typography controls are silent no-ops because selectors.typography targets .sgs-hero__headline, which edit.js sets only as an InnerBlocks TEMPLATE child's className — the generated scoped rule sits at (0,2,0) and cannot beat that child block's own inline typography at (1,0,0,0), this framework's HC2 rule. A NAIVE TEXT SEARCH CANNOT SEE THIS, proven live: it returned 2 false positives (sgs/modal, sgs/social-icons — the WP-core-generated wp-block-sgs-* root class, legitimately absent from source) and MISSED hero entirely, because .sgs-hero__headline IS present in hero's files, just never as a DOM class attribute. The rule instead resolves the effective selector, extracts the class token, and classifies via AST (InnerBlocks-template ownership) plus a DOM-emission scan excluding this codebase's CSS-selector-building idiom (_sel / 'selector' / wp_style_engine). A REAL ENGINE BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE BUILD, and it matters beyond this rule: comparing AST line numbers against ctx.cache.strippedText() line numbers is WRONG, because strippedText() blanks a multi-line comment's entire character range INCLUDING its newlines, collapsing them and shifting every subsequent line number — that silently produced ZERO findings on hero, the one block this rule exists to catch. Character OFFSETS (node.start/node.end) stay aligned between raw and stripped text; line numbers do not. strippedText() also strips only /* */ in PHP and never //, so the rule carries its own quote-aware // stripper. EXPECTED POPULATION declared before the first live run per _meta.zeroIsAClaim: 25 blocks declare supports.typography, 11 resolve to the WP-root fallback and are skipped, and of the remaining 14, 3 were predicted to flag. MEASURED: exactly 3, the same three — reconciled, no surprises. DECLARED BLIND SPOTS, stated not hidden: (1) it does NOT compute real CSS specificity, it infers child-owned-therefore-ineffective structurally from the InnerBlocks-template shape; (2) pricing-table's declared selector matches no element, but render.php pairs it with the real .sgs-pricing-table__name class in the same generated rule, so typography still visibly applies via that redundant alias — flagged anyway as a declared/rendered mismatch per F.1, and the finding text says so rather than silently downgrading; (3) the DOM-emission heuristic is text-shaped, not a PHP AST — none of the 25 live blocks hit that gap, hand-verified; (4) a selectors.typography object with disagreeing per-property selectors is not modelled (no live block does this). ADVISORY on introduction per E6 point 9; promote once the three are repaired.

rules.resolution: RESOLVED SAME COMMIT, and the resolution was NOT what the plan assumed. The plan said 'restore the marker'; investigating both findings proved the opposite. The marker was originally planted on a PanelBody/ToolsPanel pair with IDENTICAL titles (button: 'Shadow'/'Shadow'; tabs: 'Colours'/'Colours') - the genuine double-title defect. Both nestings have since been removed legitimately by the very commits that dropped the className: c5acba10 replaced button's nested ToolsPanel with a direct <ShadowControl>, and f6f3c033 replaced tabs' bespoke Colours panel with SgsColourPanel (tabs now has ZERO <ToolsPanel> in the whole file). Restoring the marker on button would have hidden an inner <h2> whose title now DIFFERS from its parent, deleting a meaningful label. So the correct repair was to delete the two orphaned CSS rules (19 lines each, pure deletions), which is what shipped. openBacklog 2 -> 0. Promotion to gate is the next step and deliberately NOT taken in the introducing commit (E6 point 9).
